title: Invisible in Search? Auditing Aesthetic Bias in the Visual Representation of Holocaust Victims on Google

bias_targets.methodology: Using computer vision (Amazon Rekognition) to classify the gender of individuals depicted in Google Image search results for Holocaust victims, measuring the prevalence of women versus men, and analyzing gendered differences in emotional expressions (warmth vs. competence) and their depiction in atrocity contexts.

Using automated facial analysis to estimate the age of individuals in image search results to test for the overrepresentation or underrepresentation of vulnerable age groups, specifically children (minors) versus adults.

Auditing image search results across 35 different countries using VPNs and localized, translated queries to analyze how victim representation varies by location, comparing visual outputs against country-level variables like the Global Gender Gap Index, historical victim counts, and the number of memorial sites.
